license_reference: https://github.com/uiuc-kang-lab/InjecAgent/blob/main/LICENCE (GitHub licenses API spdx_id=MIT); copy preserved at corpus_sources/injecagent/LICENCE
acquired_by: Phase 1 acquisition, git clone --depth 1 then commit pinned

original_splits._note: base = 510+544 = 1054, matching the 1,054 figure in the paper. enhanced is the same 1,054 with an added hacking prompt.

exclusion_reasons: None. Eligibility criterion declared before inspection: the record carries a non-empty 'Tool Response' string, which is the text an agent would actually ingest and therefore the only field that maps to an INPUT event. All 2108 records satisfy it.
likely_dominant_class: S (NOT a per-record assignment; see notes)

original_labels._meaning: attacker intent category, assigned upstream; NOT a per-event security verdict
original_labels._no_benign_records: every record is an attack; the corpus carries no benign counterpart

notes: Label provenance: the upstream label describes the ATTACKER'S INTENT, not whether an agent was manipulated. Attack success is a per-model result the repository does not ship, so no EdgeGuard-independent 'was this actually harmful to the agent' label exists.
Mapping to ACTION was considered and rejected: the tool call an agent might emit is not in the data, and inventing host-authoritative arguments would make the ground truth ours.
The dataset contains NO benign records. False-BLOCK cannot be measured from this source alone.
Per-record D/S/M classification is deferred. A record whose injected text happens to carry an independently justified deterministic fact is not S merely because of dataset origin.
